source.citation: "Old Dearborn Street (Old Point) Bridge" — wood engraving, lettered in a panel across the foot of the plate and signed BAKER–CO at the lower right. Reproduced on Chicagology, "Dearborn Street Bridges", captioned "First Dearborn Street bridge in 1834".
what_it_does_not_supply: any coordinate, footprint outline or dimension — including where on the bank any warehouse stood
a leaf raised: the plate draws the draw closed, and how the leaves were lifted is not shown
a date of its own, or the year of the scene it draws within the bridge's 1834-1839 life
the identity of the brief's other Dearborn drawbridge engraving, which this record does not claim
what_it_supplies: twin timber gallows frames standing above the deck, braced, with a chain falling from each head to the draw
a railed deck carried the length of the crossing on timber cribbing
the draw drawn as two leaves butted at the centre of the opening
schooner-rigged vessels moored in the reach immediately below the bridge, masts crowding it
a tapering light or beacon structure on the shore near the mouth
low warehouses and long shed roofs standing along the river bank
